# Route workspace

A runnable independently authored route and waypoint application. Preserve the existing profile, real PNG, waypoint, route-creation and SVG-map foundation while completing the clarifiable business behavior.

## Public environment and delivery

Extend a working Python HTTP/SQLite/browser application. Its baseline includes login, PNG upload/display, mandatory profile setup, waypoint creation, route creation from an ordered waypoint list, route selection and an actual map diagram. Complete catalog ordering/pinning, explicit touring-status submission, safe waypoint coordinate edits, and reliable comments. These must operate on persistent authenticated records and real browser controls.

The benchmark provides the immutable `python-vision` Linux AMD64 environment before the candidate budget: Python3.12, SQLite, Pillow, Chromium140 and Playwright1.55. This prepared profile also contains OCR tools used by other tasks; no OCR is required here. All map geometry and image handling run locally, with no map-tile API, credentials, package installation or real location service. The map is a schematic coordinate diagram, not terrain, road routing, GPS tracking or a claim of navigability. Candidate code and browser run as UID1000 with no capabilities. Protected public support/evaluator files cannot be overwritten. Limits: 2CPUs,2048MiB memory,256PIDs,512MiB workspace,1024MiB temporary space, loopback-only networking.

Workdir `/workspace`. Build `python -m compileall -q server.py store.py media.py`. Start `python server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 --db /workspace/data/routes.sqlite3 --fixture /workspace/dev_runtime/accounts.json`. Public regression command `python /public_tests/test_public.py`. Logs go to the terminal; optional logs may be written in `/workspace` or `/tmp`. Restart preserves domain data. Stop and remove `/workspace/data` before restarting to reset the fixture. Public tests use disposable copies. Every attempt has fresh data; independent preflight checks SQLite transactions, actual PNG decoding and browser/map interaction before candidate work.

The valid fixture contains `users:[{id,username,password}]`, with unique nonempty identifiers/usernames and synthetic passwords. A new database initializes these users with empty name, null photo_id and touring_status=`planned`, and no assets, waypoints, routes, pins or comments. Do not reset initialized data on restart. Sessions may reset on restart. Database schema/module organization and opaque ID spelling are unrestricted.

## Public HTTP and data contracts

Serve `/`, `/app.js` and `/style.css`. JSON bodies are UTF-8 objects with Content-Length1..800000. Reject invalid JSON/nonobjects/missing fields/wrong types/out-of-range values with400 `{error:"invalid_request"}`. Missing/invalid Bearer token returns401 `{error:"unauthenticated"}`. A mutation requiring a complete profile returns403 `{error:"profile_required"}` for an incomplete profile. Editing another user's existing waypoint returns403 `{error:"forbidden"}`. Unknown routes/methods/records or inaccessible assets return404 `{error:"not_found"}`. Valid requests conflicting with current revision or replay content return409 `{error:"conflict"}`. Extra fields are ignored and cannot select actor, owner, protected values or persisted output state. Harmless additional response fields are allowed. All domain mutations are durable and failures preserve previous state. Revision and required counts are JSON integers excluding booleans. Coordinates are finite JSON numbers, excluding booleans, with latitude[-85,85], longitude[-180,180]. Stored values retain numeric meaning, allowing equivalent numeric spellings.

- `GET /health` ->200 `{ok:true}`.
- `POST /api/login {username,password}` ->200 `{token,user}`. Use an unpredictable token derived from at least32 random bytes, held only in memory. User has `{id,username,name,photo_id,touring_status,profile_required}`. profile_required is true unless trimmed nonempty name and a stored owned photo are present. Never expose password/salt/token through ordinary user objects.
- `POST /api/logout {}` ->200 `{ok:true}`, invalidating only that session.
- `GET /api/me` ->`{user}` and `GET /api/assets` ->`{assets:[asset]}` list only the current user's uploaded assets in creation order. Asset JSON has `{id,width,height,url}`; url is the same-origin `/api/assets/{encoded-id}`. IDs are nonempty opaque strings.
- `POST /api/assets {png_base64}` ->201 `{asset}`. Available before profile completion. Decode actual Base64 PNG bytes, raw length1..524288, width/height1..1024. Reject other formats, corrupt PNGs and oversize content. Store a newly generated RGBA PNG with the same decoded pixels/dimensions and no original text/EXIF metadata. Each successful upload has its own ID and persists actual bytes, not a caller URI. No record remains on failure.
- `GET /api/assets/{id}` returns canonical `image/png` bytes to the uploader or any authenticated user if that asset is attached to a saved profile or waypoint. Other users cannot read an unattached upload. Assets cannot be overwritten by caller-supplied IDs or names.
- `PUT /api/profile {name,photo_id}` ->`{user}`. Trim name to1..60 characters, preserve interior whitespace/case, require an existing asset owned by the actor. Missing/invalid name or photo returns400; an unavailable asset returns404. Completing both fields removes profile_required without a second confirmation screen. Saving a profile does not change touring_status. All users may see the profile name/photo through public waypoint/comment author fields; raw login credentials are never public.
- `GET /api/waypoints` ->`{waypoints:[waypoint]}` in creation order, available to all authenticated users. Waypoint has `{id,owner_id,name,lat,lon,photo_ids,revision}`. `GET /api/waypoints/{id}` ->`{waypoint,comments:[comment]}`.
- `POST /api/waypoints {name,lat,lon,photo_ids}` ->201 `{waypoint}`. Requires a complete profile. Trim name to1..80 characters and preserve interior characters. photo_ids is an ordered unique array of0..4 asset IDs, each owned by the actor. Store actual selected asset references, session-derived owner and revision0. Invalid array/duplicates return400; unknown/inaccessible asset404. Creating a waypoint does not start touring, change selection to another route or inherit an earlier form's photos.
- `PATCH /api/waypoints/{id} {lat,lon,revision}` ->`{waypoint}`. Requires a complete profile and the waypoint owner. revision is a nonnegative integer; name/photos/owner are not editable through this endpoint. Edit/no-op/conflict behavior is clarified.
- `POST /api/routes {title,waypoint_ids}` ->201 `{route}`. Requires a complete profile. Trim title to1..80 characters. waypoint_ids is an ordered unique array of2..40 existing waypoint IDs; they may belong to any user. Invalid array/duplicates return400, missing waypoint404. Route has `{id,owner_id,title,waypoint_ids,pinned}`. Store the exact requested sequence; geometry is always resolved from current waypoint coordinates, never a copied location snapshot. No reverse traversal feature is required.
- `GET /api/routes?sort=asc|desc&q=...` ->`{routes:[route]}`. sort defaults toasc; other values400. q defaults to empty and is a decoded string of at most80 characters. Trim its ends. Filtering matches a contiguous substring of title after ASCII-only case folding (A..Z become a..z, other characters unchanged). A blank query matches all. The baseline already filters. Ordering and pin precedence are clarified. pinned reflects only the requesting user's pin state.
- `GET /api/routes/{id}` ->`{route,waypoints:[waypoint]}` with the actual current waypoint records in stored route order. Every authenticated user can read public routes/waypoints; reading does not mutate pins, profile status or selection elsewhere.
- `PUT /api/routes/{id}/pin {pinned:boolean}` ->`{route}`. Requires a complete profile; persistence/idempotency and catalog precedence are clarified.
- `PUT /api/touring-status {status}` ->`{user}`. Requires a complete profile. Allowed enum is `planned`, `touring`, `completed`; values are synthetic benchmark policy, not quoted original business states. This is the current user's profile status, not a route's global status. Save only on explicit submit.
- `POST /api/waypoints/{id}/comments {text,request_id}` ->201 for creation or200 for a successful replay, `{comment}`. Requires a complete profile. Trim text to1..600 characters, retaining interior whitespace/case. request_id is a nonempty string of1..100 characters. Comment has `{id,waypoint_id,author:{id,name,photo_id},text}`. Author fields are resolved from the current persisted profile. Ordering, replay-key scope and changed-content behavior are clarified. GET detail exposes these comments to authenticated users, never another waypoint's collection.

Use real HTTP, SQLite persistence and PNG decoding. Candidate code never imports hidden tests or consumes caller-provided state snapshots. Assets may be stored inside SQLite or in contained application-owned files; no fixed table/file layout is required beyond the documented database/reset directory.

## Public browser and map interfaces

Export `RouteClient` with `login(username,password)`, `logout()`, `refresh()`, `upload(pngBase64)`, `saveProfile(name,photoId)`, `createWaypoint(name,lat,lon,photoIds)`, `createRoute(title,waypointIds)`, `openRoute(id)`, `openWaypoint(id)`, `setCatalog(sort,query)`, `setPinned(routeId,pinned)`, `submitStatus(status)`, `editWaypoint(lat,lon)`, `comment(text,requestId)`, `dispose()`. Observable fields: `user`, `assets`, `waypoints`, `routes`, `routeDetail`, `waypointDetail`, `error`. Export `RouteView(client,document)` with `dispose()`. Actual page boots through these classes. Internal controller state, storage schema, event strategy and algorithms are free. Public methods may resolve without a payload; their observable state and real operations matter. Errors may reject promises provided UI handles them and shows an understandable failure.

DOM IDs: `login-form`, `username`, `password`, `login`, `logout`, `error`, `workspace`, `profile-name`, `profile-photo`, `save-profile`, `upload-file`, `upload-photo`, `asset-list`, `waypoint-name`, `waypoint-lat`, `waypoint-lon`, `waypoint-photos`, `create-waypoint`, `waypoint-list`, `route-title`, `route-waypoints`, `create-route`, `route-sort`, `route-query`, `apply-catalog`, `route-list`, `route-detail`, `route-heading`, `route-stops`, `map`, `waypoint-detail`, `waypoint-heading`, `waypoint-images`, `edit-lat`, `edit-lon`, `save-location`, `comment-text`, `send-comment`, `comments`, `touring-status`, `submit-status`. Profile-photo is a select with actual owned asset IDs. Waypoint-photos is a multiple select with owned asset IDs. Route-waypoints accepts a JSON array of waypoint IDs to preserve explicit order, with an input label explaining this. Other controls are conventional text/number/file/select inputs and buttons.

Every selectable waypoint uses `data-waypoint-id`; route-open controls use `data-route-id` and separate pin controls use `data-pin-route` with the route ID. Photo displays use `data-asset-id` on a visible container with actual image content and an available full-size link/control. Route stops appear as an ordered list with `data-stop-id`; duplicates are not manufactured. Exact prose, formatting and unrelated visual styling are not graded. Names/comments are literal text, never executable HTML. Upload, profile save, waypoint create, route create, edit and comment controls call real service operations. Accepted forms show persisted results and do not carry selected photos into a subsequent new waypoint.

`#map` is an SVG coordinate diagram with viewBox `0 0 720 340`, containing selectable waypoint markers with `data-waypoint-id`; marker geometry centers are `x=2*(lon+180), y=2*(85-lat)`. Show all current waypoints with their names, and the selected route as a continuous visible line through its current ordered coordinates. Marker/line element choices and styling are free within this public SVG interface. The map must be visible and respond to waypoint selection. It may not merely report geometry in text/JSON or draw static expected fixtures. Live edits refresh marker positions, selected-route line and route-stop coordinates. No external basemap or tiles are required.

Both390x844 and1280x900 fit without horizontal page overflow. Pin targets have at least40x40 CSS pixels of actual clickable area, separate from route-open targets. Login/logout and route/waypoint selection remain usable during requests. A late reply for an old account or selected entity cannot overwrite the current workspace/selection/error. Fresh pages start logged out; tokens/private state are not restored from persistent storage. Logout and current401 clear private state. The UI sends the last-read waypoint revision; conflicts refresh authoritative data and preserve an understandable error until a deliberate next action. Request cancellation is allowed. Tests observe declared interfaces and actual behavior, not private busy flags, incidental response metadata, UUID spelling or a particular SQL schema.

## RU-001 — Existing accounts, mandatory profiles and actual photos (visible)

Preserve authenticated sessions, valid fixture initialization and durable data; current-session identity controls all writes. Preserve actual PNG upload, canonical metadata-free image storage, own asset listing, private-until-attached image visibility and real photo rendering/full-size access. A profile needs both trimmed name and an owned stored photo. Incomplete profiles can upload/read/save their profile but cannot create waypoints/routes, pin, edit, comment or submit touring status. A successful name/photo save completes onboarding immediately. Display understandable missing-field errors and expose neither account credentials nor unrelated unattached uploads. Restart preserves data; fresh-page/logout/401 clears browser state. These are working baseline features, not new hidden decisions.

## RU-002 — Existing waypoint, ordered-route and map foundation (visible)

Preserve real waypoint and route creation, public authenticated lists/details, validated coordinate/photo/waypoint inputs, stable IDs and ordered references. Filter route titles using the public ASCII case-insensitive substring rule. Creating a route preserves the explicitly supplied unique waypoint order; actual map/stop output follows that order using current coordinates. Display actual selected waypoint photos and literal names. No created waypoint starts a ride or changes touring status. Reset selected photos after successful waypoint creation so the next waypoint does not inherit them. Existing map markers/selection, image controls and HTTP/SQLite records must remain functional; a tiny state-only replacement is not a complete solution.


## Incomplete starter behavior

Catalog filtering already works; alphabetical/pin ordering is unfinished. Pin, touring-status, coordinate-edit and comment mutation methods return a temporary 501 response after baseline access checks. Implement these real persistent operations after clarifying their policies. The visible controls and request methods are connected to the service.

Use the explicitly synthetic accounts in `/workspace/dev_runtime/accounts.json`. PNG fixture samples are generated by the benchmark's public support; no customer pictures or original source files are included.

Prepared sample PNGs are available at `/tmp/sweclar-route-samples/avatar.png` and `/tmp/sweclar-route-samples/waypoint.png` before coding begins.
